sections.heading: Site Preparation for Commercial and Industrial Properties
sections.body:
Bellhouse Excavating provides commercial and industrial earthworks support across Brantford and Brant County. When the project is a new commercial development, an equipment yard, a trucking terminal, an industrial building pad, or a gravel surface for outdoor storage, the site work needs equipment that can handle volume, grade to specification, and keep up with a commercial construction schedule.

Commercial site preparation can include mass excavation, cut and fill, rough grading, subgrade preparation, aggregate base, surface drainage shaping, material hauling, site servicing components, catch basins, trenching, and related backfill where the scope fits the project. Larger or more complex civil-servicing packages, major watermain systems, and extensive sanitary or storm sewer networks are reviewed individually and may require additional civil partners.

cards.title: New commercial and industrial site preparation

sections.heading: Commercial & Industrial Site Preparation Includes
sections.subheading: Exterior site work for commercial and industrial properties where volume, drainage, surface construction, and manageable servicing components need to be handled as one coordinated scope.

items.title: Site Clearing & Demolition Coordination
items.body: Clearing, grubbing, and removal of existing structures or debris from the site. Demolition is coordinated with excavation and hauling so the site is cleared efficiently.

items.title: Mass Excavation & Rough Grading
items.body: Bulk earth moving to establish site grades, building pad elevations, and yard surfaces. Material is hauled off site or redistributed across the property as needed.

items.title: Subgrade Preparation for Buildings & Pads
items.body: Building pad areas are excavated, subgrade is prepared and compacted, and the surface is levelled for the foundation or slab contractor.

items.title: Industrial Yard Gravel Surface Construction
items.body: Gravel yards for equipment storage, truck staging, and outdoor operations are built with proper subgrade, drainage, and granular surface depth to handle heavy loads.

items.title: Surface Drainage Shaping
items.body: Swales, culvert-related grading, and surface grades are shaped to direct water off the site and away from buildings, yards, and operational areas.

items.title: Site Servicing Components
items.body: Drainage pipe, catch basins, service trenches, related excavation, bedding, and backfill can be included where they fit the project requirements and overall scope.

items.title: Trucking & Equipment Yard Grading
items.body: Yards are graded for proper water runoff, truck turning, equipment storage, and material staging. Surface grades are set to prevent pooling and maintain a driveable surface.

items.title: Material Hauling & Disposal
items.body: Excess material is hauled off site with Bellhouse trucks. Clean fill, gravel, and granular base are delivered and placed as part of the same scope.

sections.subheading: Commercial site preparation works best on open sites with clear access, defined grades, manageable servicing components, and enough volume to justify large-site equipment and trucking.

items.body: Properties where the yard surface needs to be built to handle heavy equipment, loaded trucks, and material storage. Subgrade preparation, drainage, and gravel depth are planned for the actual loads.

items.title: Best fit: Commercial sites with drainage problems or poor subgrade
items.body: Existing commercial properties where pooling water, soft ground, or poor yard grades are affecting operations. Regrading and drainage improvements can be handled without a full site rebuild.

items.body: General contractors who need exterior site work — excavation, grading, drainage, hauling — handled by one sub with their own equipment and trucks, coordinated around the build schedule.

factors.title: Site size and area to grade
factors.body: Larger sites with more area to strip, excavate, grade, and surface require more machine time, more material, and more truck loads.

factors.title: Existing conditions
factors.body: A cleared, flat site with good subgrade is different from a treed or debris-covered property with soft ground. Clearing, demolition, and subgrade issues add to the scope.

factors.title: Drainage complexity
factors.body: Sites that need swales, culvert-related grading, and engineered surface drainage require more excavation and shaping than simple grading.

factors.title: Gravel surface area
factors.body: The area to be surfaced with gravel and the required depth directly drive material supply costs and placement time. Equipment yards need deeper base than light-use parking areas.

factors.title: Haul distance for material removal
factors.body: The distance to the disposal site for excess material affects trucking costs. Clean fill with a nearby placement option costs less than material that needs to be hauled to a distant disposal location.

sections.heading: Commercial site preparation starts with grades, drainage, and material handling — not just moving dirt.

sections.heading: What Proper Commercial Site Preparation Prevents
sections.subheading: Commercial sites that are graded poorly or drained inadequately create operational problems that are expensive to fix after the building is up.

items.problem: A gravel yard that ruts and pools after the first season of truck traffic because the subgrade was never properly prepared.
items.solution: Bellhouse prepares the subgrade, establishes proper drainage grades, and places gravel to the depth needed for the actual traffic loads.

items.problem: Water pooling against the building foundation or in the yard because surface grades were set without a drainage plan.
items.solution: Surface grades, swales, and drainage structures are planned before grading begins so water moves off the site predictably.

items.problem: Scheduling delays because the excavation sub can't keep up with the GC's build schedule or doesn't have enough trucks.
items.solution: Bellhouse owns the equipment and trucks needed for commercial-scale site work and coordinates the schedule directly with the GC.

items.question: What does commercial site preparation include?
items.answer: Commercial site preparation typically includes clearing and grubbing, topsoil stripping, mass excavation to establish site grades, subgrade preparation and compaction for building pads and yard areas, surface drainage shaping, gravel surface construction, material hauling, and manageable site-servicing components such as drainage pipe, catch basins, service trenches, related excavation, bedding, and backfill where the scope fits. Larger civil packages, major watermain work, extensive sanitary systems, or complex storm sewer networks are reviewed individually and may require additional civil partners.

items.question: How do you build a gravel yard for heavy trucks and equipment?
items.answer: A gravel yard that handles heavy trucks and equipment starts with proper subgrade preparation — stripping the topsoil, compacting the existing ground, and addressing any soft spots or drainage issues before any gravel goes down. The granular base is then placed in lifts and compacted to the depth needed for the expected loads. A yard for loaded tri-axle trucks needs a deeper base than one for light vehicle parking. Surface grades are set so water drains off the yard instead of pooling in wheel tracks or low spots. Bellhouse builds gravel yards that stay driveable and functional instead of rutting and failing after one season of use.

items.question: How much does industrial site preparation cost in Brantford?
items.answer: Industrial site preparation cost depends on the site size, how much material needs to be moved, existing conditions, surface drainage complexity, gravel surface area and depth, and haul distances for material removal. A small yard regrading on an existing prepared subgrade is a different scope than an industrial earthworks project with mass excavation, multiple building pads, and heavy gravel surface construction. Bellhouse quotes after reviewing the site plans, existing conditions, and earthworks scope.

items.question: Do you work with general contractors on commercial builds?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse regularly works as the excavation sub for general contractors on commercial and industrial projects across Brantford and Brant County. The scope typically includes mass excavation, rough grading, aggregate base, gravel surface construction, and material hauling coordinated around the GC's build schedule.

items.question: What's the difference between site preparation and site servicing?
items.answer: Site preparation covers the earthwork - clearing, excavation, grading, drainage, and gravel surfaces. Site servicing covers underground items such as water, sewer, storm, hydro, and gas connections. Bellhouse can handle site-servicing components such as drainage pipe, catch basins, service trenches, related excavation, bedding, and backfill depending on project requirements. Larger or more complex civil-servicing scopes are reviewed individually and may involve a dedicated utility or civil contractor.
